title: STMC: Small-Tile Multiple-Copy Compilation for Reliable Measurement-Based Quantum Computing
problem: Measurement-based quantum computing (MBQC) on photonic architectures suffers from imperfect photon control, measurement, and fusion operations; fusion failure and photon loss cause expensive circuit re-execution with significant overhead.
motivation: MBQC offers advantages like long qubit decoherence and strong scalability, but high failure rates make it impractical without mitigation techniques.
method: STMC transforms quantum circuits into fusion graphs, partitions into subgraphs, generates compact subgraph mappings for resource state layer tiles, and employs parallel tile execution with multiple copies of each subgraph.
key_novelty: Multiple-copy tile-based execution strategy to mitigate both fusion failures and photon loss in MBQC without full circuit re-execution.
contributions: Fusion graph representation and tile-based partitioning strategy
Compact subgraph mapping for resource-constrained tiles
Parallel execution of multiple copies with finish-in-order semantics
65.68× execution time speedup at 75% fusion success rate; 36.40× resource state reduction

metrics.speedup: 65.68× execution time speedup for successful circuit execution at 75% fusion success rate
metrics.area: Three orders of magnitude reduction in resource state layers; 36.40× average reduction in resource states

limitations: Evaluation on specific MBQC architectures; applicability to other quantum computing paradigms or photonic systems not explored.
